title: Three Sentenced to Combined 39.5 Years in Laredo-Linked Gun Trafficking Case
excerpt: Three people were sentenced in Del Rio to a combined 39.5 years in federal prison for smuggling more than 200 firearms into Mexico, many of them carried across the border at Laredo, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office.
content:
A federal judge in Del Rio sentenced three people to a combined 39.5 years in prison for their roles in a firearms trafficking conspiracy that moved more than 200 weapons into Mexico, many of them carried across the border at Laredo, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Texas.

Chief U.S. District Judge Alia Moses sentenced Edgar Josue Montelongo-Loera, 39, of Dallas, to 180 months in federal prison; Reymundo Hernandez-Nino, 41, to 150 months; and Kenia Lizbeth Montelongo, 31, to 144 months, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office. The sentencings took place Tuesday, Nov. 10.

According to court documents cited by the U.S. Attorney's Office, ATF agents learned in August 2024 that Kenia Montelongo had bought multiple firearms between May 17 and July 5, 2024, including seven .380-caliber pistols and a .22-caliber pistol. In the days after each purchase, she crossed into Mexico through Laredo, and Montelongo-Loera was recorded crossing in the same vehicle, according to the release.

The investigation continued through WhatsApp messages in August and November 2024 in which Montelongo-Loera discussed the trafficking operation, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office. Montelongo-Loera was arrested July 14, 2025, after a co-conspirator was caught trying to smuggle eight handguns and 19 magazines into Mexico.

Two days later, agents searched Hernandez-Nino's San Antonio home and recovered 24 firearms, including handguns, AR-15-style rifles and a shotgun, along with more than 4,000 rounds of ammunition and multiple sets of body armor, according to the release. Investigators determined the weapons, ammunition and accessories were bound for a Mexican drug cartel.

All three pleaded guilty in February 2026. U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons said the case involved ten conspirators who smuggled more than 200 weapons into Mexico, and the case was investigated by the Homeland Security Task Force as part of Operation Take Back America and prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Brett Miner.

Source: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Texas, Nov. 10, 2026.
